guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not reacting simply to Maryland’s unbeaten start. What stands out to us is the early stability of its passing game: Malik Washington has completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, while Maryland has converted 55.2 percent of its third downs and played turnover-free football in both games. That does not guarantee the same efficiency against Virginia Tech, but it supports our view that Maryland can sustain enough offense to challenge the market’s assessment.

For us, the case is less about Maryland’s rushing attack and more about Washington distributing the ball to Na’eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr., who have combined for 30 catches and 334 yards. The meaningful concern is Virginia Tech’s pass rush, which leads the FBS with 12 sacks. If Maryland protects Washington reasonably well, we think its passing-game consistency and ability to create scoring opportunities give it a credible path to outperform the market.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Virginia Tech’s rushing offense against Maryland’s front. Overton Jr. has rushed for 151 yards at 6.57 yards per carry, and our efficiency numbers identify the ground game as Virginia Tech’s clearest advantage. Maryland has allowed only 38.5 rushing yards per game through two weeks, but we do not treat that small early sample as proof that the concern is gone.

If Maryland can limit efficient runs and force passing downs, its early production of 10 sacks and an opponent third-down conversion rate of 26.9 percent becomes more relevant. If Virginia Tech consistently stays ahead of schedule on the ground, that would be the strongest challenge to our position.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12.
Maryland outgained UConn 475-223, recorded 27 first downs and held the ball for 35:31.
Maryland completed 35 of 42 passes for 350 yards and rushed 36 times for 125 yards and three touchdowns against UConn.
Maryland had two second-quarter scoring drives of more than 90 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.
Maryland's defense held UConn to 223 total yards, 67 rushing yards, 156 passing yards and 12 first downs.
Maryland recorded five sacks, forced one turnover and held UConn to 3-of-11 on third down and 0-of-2 on fourth down.
Maryland committed no turnovers and has played turnover-free football in each of its first two games.

opponent_notes.fact: Virginia Tech enters the matchup 2-0 under first-year head coach James Franklin.
Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has completed 48 of 62 passes for 551 yards and four touchdowns through two games.
Virginia Tech running back Overton Jr. has rushed for 151 yards at 6.57 yards per carry with two touchdowns.
Virginia Tech receiver Reynolds has 13 receptions for 158 yards and three touchdowns.
Virginia Tech leads the FBS with 12 defensive sacks through its first two games.

quarterback.fact: Maryland starting quarterback Malik Washington is 53-of-72 for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions through two games.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn.
Washington completed a Maryland-record 18 consecutive passes against UConn; his 82.9 percent completion rate was the fourth-highest single-game mark in program history.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and passed for 2,963 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed 4 of 5 passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards in the opener against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's starting offensive line against UConn was left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright.
Maryland changed starters at left guard from transfer Tellek Lockette against Hampton to Amory Hills against UConn; the other four offensive-line starters remained unchanged.
Rahtrel Perry has made 39 career starts, including 14 at Maryland, and owns the team's longest active offensive starting streak.
UConn starters Perry, Hills, Hershey, Howerton and Wright blocked for an offense that produced 475 yards.
Old Dominion transfer Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding has 14 receptions for 187 yards and two touchdowns through two games.
Wyoming transfer Chris Durr Jr. has 16 receptions for 147 yards and one touchdown through two games.
Gladding recorded eight receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown, while Durr recorded 10 receptions for 106 yards and a touchdown against UConn.
USC transfer Harry Dalton III rushed for career highs of 48 yards and two touchdowns against UConn.
Iverson Howard rushed 14 times for 55 yards and a touchdown and caught three passes for nine yards against UConn.
Auburn transfer Preston Howard started at tight end against UConn and caught two passes for 20 yards.

defensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's UConn defensive starters included transfer lineman Lavon Johnson, nose tackle Eyan Thomas, edge defender Nashir Taylor, linebackers Sidney Stewart, Trey Reddick and Daniel Wingate, and defensive backs Jamare Glasker, Amari Jackson, Jordan Scruggs, Messiah Delhomme and Lavain Scruggs.
Sidney Stewart recorded six tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, one sack and a forced fumble against UConn.
UCF transfer Derrick LeBlanc recorded two sacks against UConn, his first two sacks at Maryland.
Freshman linebacker Zion Elee recorded his first career sack and forced a fumble against UConn that DD Holmes recovered.
DD Holmes leads Maryland with 2.5 sacks, while Eyan Thomas and Derrick LeBlanc each have two through two games.
Daniel Wingate, Maryland's 2025 leading tackler with 102 stops, has started 26 consecutive games, the longest active defensive starting streak on the team.
Maryland added defensive linemen Lavon Johnson from Texas, Derrick LeBlanc from UCF, and Armon Parker and Jayvon Parker from Washington during the offseason.

Matt Barnes returned to Maryland as special teams coordinator after serving as Mississippi State's co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Randy Starks is Maryland's new defensive line coach, and Kyle Schmitt is the new tight ends coach.
